t: None of the funds appropriated in this Act shall be used to (1) acquire land, (2) provide for site preparation, or (3) install utilities for any family housing, except housing for which funds have been made available in annual military construction appropriation acts.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction that limits how funds may be spent on family housing. There is no tempting participation reading: it provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: None of the funds appropriated in this Act shall be used to (1) acquire land, (2) provide for site preparation, or (3) install utilities for any family housing

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that limits how appropriated money can be spent. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, comment periods, or consultation requirements mentioned.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds appropriated in this Act shall be used to (1) acquire land, (2) provide for site preparation, or (3) install utilities for any family housing, except housing for which funds have been made available in annual military construction appropriation acts.

opus.w: This section only limits what appropriated funds can be used for in family housing land acquisition, site preparation and utilities. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any decision. The reference to appropriation acts concerns Congress, which is inside the federal government, so it is not participation.
opus.s: None of the funds appropriated in this Act shall be used to (1) acquire land, (2) provide for site preparation, or (3) install utilities for any family housing
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**: it is only a limit on how appropriated money can be spent, and no one outside the federal government is involved.

1. **Tempting reading:** The mention of "annual military construction appropriation acts" might suggest some process, perhaps involving Congress.
2. **Why it fails:** Congress is inside the federal government. Beyond that, the section only restricts funding. It sets up no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a funding restriction that limits how appropriated funds can be used for family housing construction. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The text only specifies conditions for the expenditure of federal funds.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds appropriated in this Act shall be used to (1) acquire land, (2) provide for site preparation, or (3) install utilities for any family housing, except housing for which funds have been made available in annual military construction appropriation acts.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the restriction on funds implies a process where outside parties (like housing applicants or contractors) are involved, but the text itself only restricts the use of federal funds for specific construction activities. It does not describe any mechanism for public comment, consultation with non-federal entities, or advisory boards. The actors mentioned are implicit (the government spending funds), and there is no mention of outside participation in the decision-making process regarding the housing.
